newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse climbs as EMU fears dissipate.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse climbs as EMU fears dissipate.

text.p: The Madrid bourse climbed to end up on Wednesday, supported by gains in bonds and other key stock markets as EMU fears began to dissipate, dealers said.

The general index ended up 4.85 points, 0.86 pct, to 571.66, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 51.17 points, 0.79 pct, to 6,565.65. Turnover remained elevated with 110 billion pesetas changing hands.

"The market wants to revive the upward trend and although domestic fundamental support this, developments on the stability pact will be key," said one dealer. Investors are eagerly awaiting next week's EU summit for some clarification on the single currency calendar, traders said.
Dealers said they expected stocks to maintain a positive stance on Thursday.
Among individual stocks, Telefoncia slipped 15 pesetas to 4,260 after Standard & Poor's said it downgraded the firm's outlook to "negative" from "stable", maintaining its long-term "AA-" debt rating.
Among banks, BBV rose 180 pesetas to 11,240, while Santander rose five to 4,345.
